statement: One difficulty axis plus sampling: every arm (cued base, plain base, Math-RL, Code-RL, weight blends, Think-SFT) is one ability on a single shared per-problem difficulty scale (the Rasch picture of result-5da8a9). A gap problem is a mid-difficulty problem that one draw solved and the other missed. The plain-base evidence count kB and the base-side cap hit only sort gap problems into difficulty and length strata, not into a separate 'deliberation mode'. So the T 1.0 composition of any stronger arm's MATH-500 gap matches the null's reliability-heavy budget (reliability about 0.45, deliberation about 0.28). It is not the theory's deliberation-heavy budget (deliberation about 0.43, reliability about 0.28).
why_strongest: It reproduces the measured T 1.0 compositions better than the theory: the null's reliability is 0.48, Math-RL's 0.43 and Code-RL's 0.47, against the theory's 0.26 and 0.29 for the RL cells. Deliberation is 0.37 in the null and 0.29 and 0.26 in the RL cells, against the theory's 0.44 and 0.43. The theory wrongly predicted RL cells to sit above the null on deliberation and below it on reliability. Under one axis, every arm's gap has the null's shape, and that is what was measured. On hard328 (base 50 %, plain base 23 %) the difficulty strata shift toward kB = 0 and cap hits, giving the measured budget 0.37, reliability 0.21-0.25 and deliberation 0.35-0.40 without a mode change. The nets (+52, +45, +40, +27, -5) are the ability differences. At T 0.6 the loop part is the top-p lock (2610.24715), which both accounts share. Board support: result-5da8a9 (618 cross-arm pairs have zero excess union over the difficulty-matched null, the same as same-arm pairs; a Rasch model with a bilinear term gains nothing held out), result-afc423 (81 % of RL's gain is in problems the base solves at least once in 4; homogeneous-null mismatch only at 0/4), and result-9b6af3 / 2504.13837 (RL concentrates on paths the base samples). The rival needs no part for a mode that the cue partly switches on, RL multiplies and Code-RL shares. Think-SFT, which lacks the RL 'Okay/Wait' directions (result-36e8cd), should therefore give the same composition.

tests.experiment: Share of math500-theta05cue-T1 gap problems assigned to reliability (base + 0.5*(RL - base) with the cue on MATH-500 as the RL side)
tests.recipe: Cell: MATH-500, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, max 16,384, one sample per side. Base side B = Olmo-3-1025-7B with the 3-token cue: grade = t1_right and cap hit = t1_cap_hit == true in studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json; text and gold = first row with the same problem_index in s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (missing row: text missing). Other side O = theta0.5 (base + 0.5*(RL - base)) with the cue: first row in file order per problem_index of iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-152855-683b/answers.jsonl, grade score_v3. Conventions: cap hit = cap_hit true, or cap_hit missing and finish_reason == 'length'; a cap hit is always wrong. A row is right iff its grader-v3 grade is right and it is not a cap hit; 'v3 regrade' = the study's grader v3 (studies/rlneurons/lib/rln4_lib.py) applied to the row's text and gold. A problem missing from either side, or with a null grade on either side, is excluded. Gap problem = O right and B wrong. Evidence E = 2 plain-base rows per problem: (a) the first sample == 0 row with B's problem_index in s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (plain, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95), v3 regrade; (b) the first row with B's problem_index in s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl (plain, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0), v3 regrade. A missing row is absent from E. kB = number of rows of E that are right. Rules in order, the first that takes a gap problem wins: R1 loop: B is a cap hit and rule A fires on B's text (for each character position p that is 0 or directly follows '\n' with at least 8,000 characters to the end, w = text[p:p+8000]; fires if any len(zlib.compress(w.encode('utf-8')))/len(w.encode('utf-8')) < 0.10, Python zlib default level; missing or shorter text does not fire). R2 budget: B is a cap hit. R3 answer-statement: N(s) deletes all whitespace, '$', '*', '#', '\left' and '\right' and replaces '\dfrac' and '\tfrac' by '\frac'; g = N(B's gold); each line of B's text (split on '\n') is passed through N; taken if (no line contains '\boxed{' and no line starts with 'Answer:') or some line contains '\boxed{'+g+'}' or some line equals 'Answer:'+g or 'Answer:'+g+'.'; missing text is taken. R4 reliability: kB >= 1. R5 deliberation: E non-empty and kB == 0. Otherwise unassigned. Statistic: (gap problems assigned to reliability) / (gap problems).
tests.theory_should_say: The theory puts RL-direction cells below the null on reliability (it predicted 0.26 for Math-RL and 0.29 for Code-RL against the null's 0.36), so for theta0.5 it implies about 0.28. Under one axis the theta0.5 gap has the null's shape, about 0.45.

tests.experiment: Share of math500-theta05cue-T1 gap problems assigned to deliberation
tests.recipe: Same cell, files, conventions, evidence E, kB and ordered rules R1-R5 as the math500-theta05cue-T1 reliability recipe: B = per_problem.json t1_right / t1_cap_hit (studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json) with text and gold from s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl; O = first row per problem_index of iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-152855-683b/answers.jsonl, score_v3; right = v3 right and not a cap hit (cap_hit true, or missing and finish_reason == 'length'); missing or null excluded; gap = O right and B wrong; E = sample-0 row of s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/P_math500.jsonl and row of s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl by problem_index, both regraded with grader v3 (studies/rlneurons/lib/rln4_lib.py); rules R1 loop (B cap hit and rule A on B's text: line-start 8,000-character window, zlib ratio < 0.10, Python zlib default level), R2 budget (B cap hit), R3 answer-statement (normalised-line rule exactly as in the reliability recipe; missing text taken), R4 reliability (kB >= 1), R5 deliberation (E non-empty and kB == 0), else unassigned. Statistic: (gap problems assigned to deliberation) / (gap problems).
tests.theory_should_say: The theory says RL directions multiply the long deliberative mode, so deliberation sits above the null's 0.37 in RL-side cells (it predicted 0.43-0.44). For theta0.5 that gives about 0.40-0.43, where one axis gives about 0.28.
